clue.text: Extremely odd inversion reported to exceed in importance

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so we want what the swapped phrase sounds like when said

parts.note: extremely odd is way out; inverting that phrase swaps its two halves round

explanation.surface: Some strangely backwards arrangement is said to matter more than anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inversion' looks like a noun in the surface, but here it swaps WAY OUT, the slang for extremely odd, to OUT WAY before it is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To outweigh something is to be greater than it in importance or value.

clue.text: People dedicated to religion have quiet role model with identity like that of the earth

parts.note: oblates are laypeople or religious dedicated to a monastic life
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a hero is someone looked up to as a model
ID is the usual short form of identity

explanation.surface: Devout people keep a low profile, imitate their idols and share an identity with the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the earth's shape: it is a sphere slightly flattened at the poles.
explanation.definitionFit: The earth's figure is a slightly squashed sphere, the shape geometers call this name.

clue.text: Two prizes coming up for the upper class

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up turns each word so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: a pot is the prize money in a game
a reward is a prize given for an achievement

explanation.surface: Two awards are being handed out to the aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns each prize in place: POT gives the first word and REWARD the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Top drawer is an idiom for the highest social class, the best people.

clue.text: In which Arnie and Reg'll get involved with Netta, say

definitions.text: In which Arnie and Reg'll get involved with Netta, say

indicators.note: the names are mixed up together, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scenario in which two men and a woman become entangled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get involved' rearranges the letters of ARNIE, REGLL and NETTA; the result names the three-way love affair the surface describes.
explanation.definitionFit: An eternal triangle is a romantic entanglement of three people, such as two men and one woman.

clue.text: German isn't common — he's probably Welsh

parts.note: ain't is the informal, non-standard form of isn't

explanation.surface: A German bloke doesn't seem ordinary: he is likely from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Geraint is a Welsh first name, known from the Arthurian knight; 'common' marks ain't as vulgar speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Geraint is a traditionally Welsh man's name, so its bearer is likely Welsh.

clue.text: In the present circumstances the fool must eat one at half-time

indicators.note: the fool's word is to swallow the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: an ass is a fool
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: half of time is its first two letters

explanation.surface: The jester has to have a bite to eat at the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-time' looks like the interval of a match; here 'half' works on 'time' alone, and 'at' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: As it is means things being the way they currently are.

clue.text: It's impossible to put an article between figures

indicators.note: the article is placed in the middle, between the two shapes

parts.note: a square is a geometric figure
a circle is a geometric figure
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Placing a piece of writing amid some numbers cannot be done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' looks like numbers, but means two geometric shapes; THE goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To square the circle is an idiom for attempting something impossible, from the insoluble geometry problem.

clue.text: Capable of going fast forward when surrounded by sheep

indicators.note: the word for forward sits inside the word for sheep

parts.note: a tup is a ram
on means forward, as in moving on

explanation.surface: Something that can speed ahead while in the middle of a flock.
explanation.walkthrough: TON-UP is British slang for reaching a hundred miles an hour, typically a motorcyclist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ton-up describes a motorcyclist or machine able to reach a hundred miles an hour.

clue.text: Get over being led astray in pursuit of fiddle

indicators.note: following means the rearranged word comes after the instrument

parts.note: a Strad (Stradivarius) is a famous violin

indicators.note: led astray is led off course, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Recover from being misled after a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests cheating; it is the violin STRAD, followed by DLE, the anagram of LED from 'astray'.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle a fence or obstacle is to get over it with one leg either side.

clue.text: Threaten devil with death

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
end can mean death, as in meeting one's end

explanation.surface: Make menacing gestures at a demon with a fatal outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To impend is to loom or threaten as something about to happen.

clue.text: Fall from grace from revolutions and drug

parts.note: laps are circuits or revolutions of a track
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Disgrace that comes from going round in circles and taking narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or decline from good conduct.

clue.text: Smuggler of strange racehorse?

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
a runner is a horse taking part in a race

explanation.surface: Asking whether a peculiar horse is a smuggler.
explanation.walkthrough: A rum-runner smuggled alcohol, typically during American Prohibition; the surface pretends the horse is odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum-runner was a person or ship smuggling liquor illegally.

clue.text: Bully misprinted as "satyr nine"

indicators.note: a misprint has the letters wrong, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tormentor's name appears with a typo as a mythical goat-man and a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misprinted' rearranges the letters of SATYR NINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tyrannise is to bully or domineer cruelly over others.

clue.text: Swift and quiet in attack

indicators.note: the letter for quiet sits inside the word for attack

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A fast and silent assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and swift are synonyms meaning very fast.

clue.text: Lean back to embrace West Indian in the dusk

indicators.note: the turned word holds the abbreviation inside it
back means the word for lean is read in reverse

parts.note: to tilt is to lean
WI is the abbreviation for West Indian or West Indies

explanation.surface: Reclining and hugging a Caribbean companion as evening falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for lean before it is opened up; 'in the dusk' is an adjectival phrase, matching the answer's part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit means lit by twilight, which is the dim light of dusk.

clue.text: Doing what one should to turn tea (say) into fluid

annotationWithheld.why: Doing what one should to turn tea (say) into fluid (7): DUTIFUL is FLUID plus U and T; T is tea said aloud, but no parse finds the U and an anagram indicator without 'fluid' doing two jobs (fodder and indicator)
annotationWithheld.clue: Doing what one should to turn tea (say) into fluid

clue.text: Anticipate a lot of trees — without exception

parts.note: a forest is a large area covered with trees
all means every one, with no exceptions

explanation.surface: Expect a great many trees, every single one.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act in anticipation and so prevent something.

clue.text: See 1
Picture wine with fish

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Imagine a dish of fish served with wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or picture someone or something.

clue.text: He does what he's told, giving Scots little money outside

indicators.note: the money word goes round the outside of the Scots word

parts.note: the yen is Japanese currency
sma is Scots for small

explanation.surface: An obedient fellow tips the Scots some small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' belongs to 'Scots', not to 'money': SMA is the Scottish word for small.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man always agrees with and obeys his superiors.

clue.text: Make a mistake filling cast with wine

indicators.note: the error word fills the middle of the word for cast

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Slip up while pouring a sherry into a mould.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests actors or a mould; here it is SHY, to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from southern Spain.

clue.text: Genuine error with part of the brain

parts.note: a sin is a moral error

indicators.note: only part of the brain's name is used, its end dropped

parts.note: the cerebrum is the main part of the brain

explanation.surface: A real mistake made with a portion of one's grey matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' cuts CEREBRUM down to CERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means honest and genuine in feeling.

clue.text: Newspaperman to ride out of place

indicators.note: the letters are moved out of their places, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A journalist has to go riding away from where he should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' rearranges the letters of TO RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a senior journalist in charge of a newspaper.

clue.text: Heath's girl

definitions.meaning: heath here is the plant, the heather genus of that name

explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, and also a woman's name.

clue.text: Picture 1,000 years old?

parts.note: read as one and a thousand: I is the Roman one and M the Roman thousand
age is how many years old one is

explanation.surface: A painting a millennium old.
explanation.walkthrough: '1,000' is read in two parts: the 1 gives I and the thousand gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness of something.

clue.text: Ruined? Change sides and get poetically tanned?

parts.note: sunk means ruined, as in done for

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of sides

explanation.surface: After being ruined, switch teams and get a romantic suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change sides' reads like swapping teams at half-time, but 'Change' is an anagram signal working on 'sides' alone; 'poetically' marks the answer as a literary flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sun-kissed is a poetic, flattering way of saying tanned by the sun.

clue.text: Primate to dodge being minus 5 for drink

parts.note: an orang is an orang-utan, a primate

indicators.note: minus 5 means the Roman numeral for five is taken away

parts.note: to evade is to dodge

explanation.surface: An ape avoids losing five points for a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: V is the Roman numeral 5; removing it from EVADE leaves EADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a sweet drink flavoured with orange.

clue.text: Freewheel to the seaside

definitions.meaning: to move along without power or pedalling
the shore where land meets sea

explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to freewheel downhill; the coast is the seaside.

clue.text: It comes to an end when electrification begins

definitions.text: It comes to an end when electrification begins

parts.note: dies means stops or comes to an end

indicators.note: begins takes the opening letters of electrification

explanation.surface: Something that is finished once the electric railway arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'begins' takes the first two letters, EL. Diesel locomotives were replaced as railways were electrified.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel trains are phased out when a railway line is electrified.

clue.text: Lilburne's plane?

parts.note: John Lilburne led a 17th-century English radical movement for equality; a plane is a tool that makes a surface flat

explanation.walkthrough: The Levellers were a radical faction in the English Civil War, led by John Lilburne; a carpenter's plane flattens wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of Lilburne's radical party bore this name, and a plane is a tool that makes surfaces flat.
